source_text: III. Ἀλλὰ χάρις τῷ θεῷ· κατὰ πάντων γὰρ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν. Ὃ γὰρ γενναιότατος Γερμανικὸς ἐπερρώννυεν αὐτῶν τὴν δειλίαν διὰ τῆς ἐν αὐτῷ ὑπομονῆς· ὃς καὶ ἐπισήμως ἐθηριομάχησεν. Βουλομένου γὰρ τοῦ ἀνθυπάτου πείθειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντος τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ κατοικτεῖραι, ἑαυτῷ ἐπεσπάσατο τὸ θηρίον προσβιασάμενος, τάχιον τοῦ ἀδίκου καὶ ἀνόμου βίου αὐτῶν ἀπαλλαγῆναι βουλόμενος. Ἐκ τούτου οὖν πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, θαυμάσαν τὴν γενναιότητα τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς καὶ θεοσεβοῦς γένους τῶν Χριστιανῶν, ἐπεφώνησεν· Αἶρε τοὺς ἀθέους· ζητείσθω Πολύκαρπος.
thought_title: Germanicus encourages the fearful and turns the crowd toward Polycarp
orientation: The Smyrnaean writers are showing how some Christians endured torture while Germanicus provoked the beast and the crowd demanded Polycarp.
pass_a_gloss: But thanks to God; for he did not have strength against all. For the very courageous Germanicus was strengthening their fearfulness through the endurance in him; who also fought wild beasts in a notable manner. For while the proconsul was wishing to persuade him and saying to pity his youth, he drew the beast upon himself by forcing it, wishing to be released more quickly from their unjust and lawless life. Therefore on account of this the whole crowd, having marveled at the courage of the race of the Christians beloved by God and revering God, shouted: Take away the godless people; let Polycarp be searched for.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes this office as proconsul
brief glossary fixes ἄθεοι as godless people and αἶρε is a removal command by the crowd
third-person passive imperative expresses demanded search, not yet arrest

choices.english: fought wild beasts in a notable manner
choices.why: adverb marks public conspicuousness of the act, not moral nobility

pass_b_english: But thanks be to God: he did not prevail against them all. The most courageous Germanicus gave them strength in their fear by the endurance within him. He also fought the wild beasts in a notable way. The proconsul wanted to persuade him and told him to pity his own youth, but Germanicus forced his way forward and drew the beast upon himself, because he wanted to be released the sooner from their unjust and lawless life. So the whole crowd marveled at the courage of the God-loving and God-fearing people of the Christians and shouted, "Take away the godless people," and, "let Polycarp be searched for."

problems.why: The Greek says Germanicus braced the others' timidity, steadying the fearful. 'Gave strength to their fear' reads as if he made the fear stronger.
problems.fix: gave strength to their timid ones by the endurance within him

edits.old: gave strength to their fear by the endurance within him
edits.new: gave them strength in their fear by the endurance within him

fixed: Fixed 'gave strength to their fear' — ἐπερρώννυεν αὐτῶν τὴν δειλίαν means he steadied the fearful, not made fear stronger — to 'gave them strength in their fear'.
